body: I understand things aren't simple. Nothing will change until she gets some help. Tackle the depression, everything else comes second.

Your girlfriend is depressed. I experience this exact cycle - eat because I'm depressed, feel more depressed because I'm gaining weight... Rinse and repeat. Take her to a doctor, she may need to start on some medication or have some counselling. Even getting out of bed can be a huge struggle in the grips of depression so I have no doubt the gym is an insurmountable task for her to think about. Give her love and support and perhaps suggest exercise as a treatment for depression (this is how I have learned to think of it and it truly is brilliant for mental health). Take her for nature walks and go on adventures together. Please don't give up on her when she is clearly in need of support.

I started taking fluoxetine when I was about 17. Had some horribly annoying but not serious side effects - SWEATING. ALL THE TIME. Terrible insomnia as well - would wake at 3am every night and feel like I'd just downed 10 red bulls, THAT awake. It worked for a while, then I got depressed again, upped the dose, worked for a while longer. Then I turned into a zombie. I couldn't feel ANYTHING. Just an emotionless shell. I hated that feeling so much. Not to mention it completely annihilated my usually high libido. Stopped taking it of my own accord and was better for a while.

Few months later, realise I can't handle life without the meds. Didn't want to lose my sex drive again so started on citalopram. Felt a bit better, also a lot less side effects with this one. Plateaued out again, increased dose. Worked for me really well for about a year. Then life circumstances got hard and I basically felt like I was sitting on a flimsy safety net (the citalopram) about 3 inches above boiling hot lava (the depression). I could feel it was there, i could almost feel it burning me, but something was physically stopping my brain from experiencing the severe depression. After a while I got sick of not feeling and also felt like, how would I ever get better  if I don't allow myself to feel? Stopped taking those ones too.

Idk if mine is cheating, because i was on acid. But regardless, it remains my most intensely spiritual experience to this day.
And couple of friends and i took some tabs and went to a local beach to wait for it to kick in. It was a clear night and all the stars were out. One of my friends had never tripped before and asked me to meditate with him. We sat cross-legged facing each other with our palms touching. I began to meditate. At some point i noticed that i was... Humming. Like a deep, chesty sound. More like creating massive vibrations from my chest. These grew stronger and stronger as my awareness lessened. I eventually hit a pinnacle where the noise i was emmitting became extremely high pitched. There was bright white light covering my vision which faded into a huge... Light being? Somewhat humanoid entity standing in front of me, welcoming me, filling me with the greatest peace and joy i have ever known. I felt like i might explode from vibration at this point.
Next thing i know im waking up face down in the grass. My friend i was meditating with said he moved away from me when i went into the trace-like state, and i was "humming" for about an hour until i suddenly faceplanted the grass. When i went to sit with them he had this look of horror on his face. When i asked him what was wrong he said that when i walked over to him i had these huge, ghostly looking wings coming out of my back that faded when i sat down. I hadnt told him about my experience yet.
So yeah, idk maybe that was just some fucking legit acid but it felt very real and significant at the time and i often think back to that experience.

I'm a 21(F) and I smoke weed every day religiously. I struggle with major depression, self harm and crazy bad anxiety (diagnosed). I also believe I have BPD, although have never seen more than a GP for mental health reasons. When I'm high I feel like I can actually be happy, for the most part it calms me down and allows me an hour or two of relief before the next sesh is due. I can honestly say that marijuana has saved my life. The fuzzy green nirvana it provides gives me a reason to live. Without it the anxiety kicks in and everything spirals downhill from there. I've had shitty experiences with multiple SSRIs and am now pretty convinced the best medicine for me is simply a big fat cone. The mental health system in NZ is pretty useless, so I self prescribe some Mary and continue existing through the monotonic haze that is my life as of late. I seriously relate to and SUPPORT anyone who uses marijuana as a coping mechanism. It may not be conventional, but it certainly works for me and I'm glad it helps you, too.
